correctness.rationale: For every \(L,d,\kappa>0,r>1\), the quadratic form gives a simple principal eigenvalue. On the positive Neumann–Dirichlet subinterval the left and right one-sided impedances satisfy \(\ell_x=\lambda+\ell^2/D\), \(m_x=-\lambda-m^2/D\), and \((\ell+m)_x=(\ell^2-m^2)/D\), forcing a unique balanced global minimizer at fixed \(\lambda\); competitors outside this subinterval admit an inexpensive side-supported trial function. Monotone dependence of the required strength on \(\lambda\) yields the unique fixed-strength maximum. Exact two-layer phases give the \(z\) equation and location. The decreasing derivative \(lpha_r\prime\) proves monotone movement; its large-contrast limit leads to the unique \(	an t=-t\) root and sharp bound. Independent transfer matrices passed 2578 diagnostic assertions on the final packaged checker; finite checks are not substitutes for proof.

value.rationale: The exact constrained location of one partially reactive point target in stratified transport is naturally motivated by maximizing long-time absorption, and heterogeneity makes the answer genuinely different from the centered homogeneous optimum. The sharp dimensionless lower-bound constant applies uniformly across unbounded material contrast and trap strength, and the explicit weak/strong reactivity movements provide interpretable design limits. This is not a trivial rescaling or a known-table recomputation; independent verification of historical priority is not claimed.
